headline.process: Rainfall-associated change is not merely amplification or marginal detection. Previously silent cells enter overlapping/full chorus states, and recruited species deepen to third and later occupied stops.
headline.memory: The rainfall-associated route-new incidence signal is overwhelmingly recurrent acoustic activity from species already observed in prior years, especially at the same physical SiteID. Prior-only strong-chorus activation shows the same local acoustic memory.
headline.spatial_structure: Spatial depth increases beyond the second stop, but conditional on occupied-stop count there is no convergent evidence that occupied stops are unusually geographically clustered.
headline.habitat: NWI hydroperiod and broad Palustrine versus Riverine/Lacustrine context do not explain the robust strong-chorus activation signal.
headline.generality: The signal is diffuse across many taxa and robust to omitting any single state, but state-specific slopes are heterogeneous and cross-continental universality remains unestablished.

spatial_diagnostics.interpretation: The extra occupied stops are not convincingly arranged into unusually tight clusters after conditioning on k and route geometry.

geography.interpretation: No single state drives the pooled effect, but the magnitude and even direction vary substantially among states.

wetland_context.interpretation: Mapped long-term wetland regime/system does not identify where rainfall-associated strong chorus activation occurs.

falsified_or_weakened: simple social-cue attraction to already-active stops
NWI hydroperiod as the strong-chorus mediator
Palustrine versus Riverine/Lacustrine wetland system as the strong-chorus mediator
one or a few taxa as the sole driver
literal appearance of entirely novel route/site records as the main source of rainfall recruitment
remaining_mechanistic_candidates: behavioural/reproductive reactivation of locally persistent populations whose acoustic activity is intermittent across years
multi-cue gating by rainfall together with temperature/season or unmeasured atmospheric moisture
fine-scale hydrological state not captured by long-term NWI wetland class
physiological hydration effects not reducible to mapped wetland context

external_generality.conclusion: North American robustness is strong; a universal cross-continental law is not established.
